BaffoonMC Encyclopedia

Every character and unique being on the server: who they are, where to find them, what they want from you, and what they say. Heaven sits where the End used to be, Moloch's realm takes the Nether's place, and the Overworld has its bad nights.

The Realms

BaffoonMC has three worlds. The Overworld is home. The End has become Heaven, where God holds court. The Nether is gone: in its place is Moloch’s realm, a burning land of rings around his pyramid.

HeavenTakes the End’s placeReached through the Gate of Heaven, the stronghold’s portal room
End portal←
The OverworldHomeWhere you build, farm, claim land and live
Any portal→
Moloch’s RealmTakes the Nether’s placeEvery portal arrives on the roads to his pyramid

Moloch’s Realm, ring by ring

The realm is one great circle. Everything starts at the pyramid in the middle, and every ring further out is wilder, emptier and older, until the Wall closes it off about 6,900 blocks from the temple.

Getting in
Light any portal in the Overworld. They all lead to one arrival point at the start of the Sacred Way, facing the pyramid. There’s no 1:8 travel and no Nether.
Getting out
Walk through the Exit Gate behind the arrival point. It takes you back to the portal you came through. Portals can’t be lit inside the realm.
The sky
Always the same: a red, smoky dusk, with fog closing in past a few chunks. You can set your spawn here with a bed or a respawn anchor.
Monsters
The realm’s own: blazes, magma cubes, piglins, wither skeletons, ghasts and worse, depending on how far out you go. Nothing spawns in the light, or within 400 blocks of the temple.
Moloch’s Hunger
It fills with sacrifices and offerings thrown into the summit fire. When it’s full, Moloch rises five minutes later and everyone fights him together.

  1. The Temple

    0 – about 250 blocks

    The great pyramid, banded red and black, with stairs on all four sides up to the summit fire pit. The plaza and moat around it are calm: nothing spawns there by itself, and no other structures generate within 400 blocks. Moloch sleeps in the battle hall underneath.

    Summit fire pitBattle hallSafe grounds

  2. The four roads

    Out to 1,200 blocks

    The Sacred Way and its three sister roads run straight out from the pyramid along the compass lines. Every portal arrives at the start of a road, next to an Exit Gate home. The roads are holy ground: nobody can build, dig or burn on them.

    Arrival pointsExit GatesCan’t be changed

  3. The Terraces

    180 – 800 blocks

    Stepped land in three moods: Soul Terraces of soul sand, nether wart and blue soul fire; Crimson Terraces of red fungus forest; Ash Terraces of grey ash and open flame. Rivers of lava run out along the four diagonals.

    Soul, crimson and ashLava canals

  4. Basalt Crown

    800 – 2,600 blocks

    A wide land of basalt pillars around the inner realm. This is where the realm’s scattered places turn up: Blood Altars, Golden Calves and Moloch’s fortresses, never closer than 500 blocks to the temple.

    Blood AltarsGolden CalvesFortresses

  5. Crater Fields

    2,600 – 3,800 blocks

    Broken, pitted ground, scarred with craters, some of them pooled with lava. The first of the outer rings, and the start of the long walk to the edge.

    CratersLava pools

  6. Lake of Fire

    3,800 – 4,500 blocks

    A ring of lava all the way round the realm, broken by islands and rough causeways. Old bones lie half-sunk along its shores. Bring Fire Resistance.

    IslandsCausewaysBone remains

  7. Titan Wood

    4,500 – 5,500 blocks

    A dead forest of enormous trees, blood-red trees and giant mushrooms, over a floor of ash, roots and bone heaps instead of water.

    Titan treesBlood treesGiant mushrooms

  8. Basalt Deltas

    5,500 – 6,000 blocks

    The land of the giants. Their footprints are pressed into the basalt, their swords stand where they fell, and their campfires still burn among glowstone and scattered remains.

    Giant footprintsGiant swordsGiant campfires

  9. The Wall

    6,000 – about 6,900 blocks

    Jagged cliffs rise higher and higher until they close off the realm completely. There is nothing beyond. This is the edge of Moloch’s world.

    The edge

Feeding the fire

Moloch only eats what’s precious in his world. Throw these into the summit fire pit to fill his Hunger. Anything else is spat back out. Sacrifices fill it too: see Kidnapping.

0.2%Redstone dust
1.8%Block of redstone
10%Enchanted golden apple
30%The World Egg, from Heaven

Heaven at a glance

The End, remade. Reach it through the Gate of Heaven, the gilded portal room in every stronghold.

God’s island

  • Where everyone arrives, and where God holds court.
  • Protected: nobody can build, break or claim land here.
  • Beat God and the World Egg appears. Whoever grabs it first keeps it.

The Seven Heavens

  • The outer islands, over the void.
  • You float (Slow Falling) and dig slowly (Mining Fatigue III).
  • Sleep in a bed and God carries you back to His island.
  • Zephyrs, Brimstone Cubes and Cloud Cotton fields. Claims are allowed.

The End, remade as God's realm

Heaven

The ender dragon is gone. In its place God holds court on the main island, and the Seven Heavens drift around Him on the outer islands. Visitors float and dig slowly out there, so nobody settles.

God

The Ancient of Days, and a disappointed grandad

Found
On His throne by the exit portal, on the End's main island
Takes the place of
The ender dragon
Health
Grows with the crowd: 1,600 against one fighter, 4,400 against five, 7,900 against ten
Rewards
God's Halo for the top fighter, pieces of the Vestments of the Ancient, and the World Egg

A giant, grey-bearded old man in white robes, with a halo and an old man's voice. He is in no hurry to fight. On the first day He sits on His throne making small talk, until someone hits Him or tells Him they've come to challenge Him.

His fight is the Seven Days of Creation. A new Day starts each time He loses another seventh of His health. On the second Day He rises and swims through the sky, lifting people into the air (Rapture). On the third He calls down two Archangels. The fourth brings falling stars and the Pillar of Salt, which freezes anyone who looks at Him. On the fifth, angels swoop in, and He marks everyone who has been feeding Moloch. By the sixth He has lost His temper and throws His throne. On the seventh He keeps nodding off: hit Him while He sleeps for double damage, and He wakes up furious.

Smite, a pillar of light followed by lightning, runs through every Day, so keep moving. Leave Him alone and He heals, but never back past the start of the Day He's on. His damage grows 15% with each Day.

  • <God> Ah. Visitors. Wipe your feet.
  • <God> Challenge ME? I invented challenges.
  • <God> Back in my day the meek inherited the earth. Now they just hit me with swords.
  • <God> GET OFF MY LAWN!
  • <God> I WASN'T ASLEEP!

Archangels

Judgement, in two forms

God’s host comes in two forms. The shells guard Heaven from the first day; the wings only come out once someone has beaten Him.

The shell

Shulkers

Found
Across the End, on God’s island and out on the Seven Heavens, from the start
Danger
One hit from their bolt of judgement kills. A Totem of Undying can still save you
Looks
An ivory shell with a gold rim and a golden spiral on its base

The wings

Ghasts

Found
Only once God has been beaten, drifting round the Seven Heavens at least 800 blocks from the centre. Never on the main island
Danger
Their fireball smites like the shell’s bolt. Up to two around each player, and they spot you from 48 blocks
Fighting back
20 hearts each. Hit a fireball back at one and it takes 5 hearts: four returns bring it down
Drops
Sometimes (15%) a Dried Angel. Soak it to raise a Happy Angel
Leaves alone
Anyone Graced by the Angel Engine

On the third Day of His fight, God calls two Archangels down to help, and they fight for Him even against the Graced.

  • <God> Archangels! Attend me.
  • <God> I brought help. Don't tell anyone.
  • <God> My host. Be polite, they bite.

The Peacekeeper

Heaven's doorman, and its only shop

Found
Keeping watch by the Pearly Gates
Made from
A great, still vex, more than twice the usual size
Trades
The Heavenly Respirator for 2 Tears of God, frames for a Gate of Heaven for 1 Tear, Levitation splash potions for 10 diamonds, and the Angel Engine for the World Egg

A pale vex that never moves from its post and never draws a blade. It trades with whoever comes up to Heaven.

Its most important stock is the Angel Engine, the Heart of Darkness mended in gold. It is the only cure for the inhuman, and the inhuman can never come up here to buy it, so someone else has to carry it down to them. Eaten by anyone else, it Graces them for good: undead take more damage from them, the Archangel ghasts leave them be, and a Second Wind of Regeneration lifts them when they fall low.

  • <Peacekeeper> Breathe easy. The air up here was made for you too.

Zephyrs

The winds of Heaven

Found
Roaming the outer islands of the Seven Heavens
Made from
Breezes
Never
Near God's island, or while His fight is on

Breezes that roam the outer islands. Their wind charge hits harder than a breeze's and lifts you off your feet with Levitation. Heaven's own Slow Falling lets you back down gently, as long as there's an island under you when it does.

Like natural mobs they come and go: a couple per player at most, gone once nobody is near.

Brimstone Cubes

Hell's sulfur, drifted up to Heaven

Found
The outer islands of the Seven Heavens, at least 300 blocks out from God's island
Made from
Sulfur cubes, grown three times their size
Never
Near God's island, or while His fight is on

Lumps of Hell's sulfur that drifted up into the Seven Heavens and swelled big enough to hold a person. They spot you from 24 blocks away and hop after you, steering in mid-air. Up close they pounce, aiming at where you're running to, not where you are.

If one lands on you, it swallows you whole: three seconds stuck inside while it burns you (two hearts a second), then it spits you out in a random direction. Sometimes that's over the void, and Heaven's Slow Falling is all that gives you time to save yourself.

They have 40 health, and you can't bucket, shear or feed them. Like the Zephyrs they come and go: one per player at most, gone once nobody is near.

Takes the Nether's place

Moloch's Realm

Every Overworld portal leads to one arrival point at the start of the Sacred Way, facing the great pyramid. The only way back is the Exit Gate behind you. Moloch sleeps under the pyramid, and his Hunger grows with every sacrifice.

Moloch

The idol under the pyramid

Found
The battle hall under the pyramid, once his Hunger is full
Made from
A warden three times the size, reskinned as a horned bronze idol with a furnace for a belly
Health
Grows with the crowd: 1,500 against one fighter, 4,300 against five, 11,300 against fifteen
Rewards
Moloch's Horns for whoever hurt him most, and pieces of Moloch's Regalia

His Hunger fills from 0 to 100 with sacrifices and offerings. When it's full he rises five minutes later, and everyone is called to the arena to fight him together, with 30 minutes on the clock. Once he's summoned his hall is sealed: anyone can walk in, nobody walks out. Whoever dies in the hall rises as a ghost and has to watch until it's over.

Between ordinary warden blows he picks from the bull charge, the leap slam, the Cross of Fire, furnace breath, the fire ring and the chain pull, which drags in anyone hanging back. If you dodge his charge so he hits a pillar, he topples over, stunned and open. Arrows only do half damage, and his Soulfire Ward burns them and throws fire back.

At 75% his golden champions, piglin brutes, shield him until they're dead. At 50% he screams. At 25% he collapses and feeds. Below that he's in a frenzy. If the fighters lose, they carry Moloch's Curse for 15 minutes: Weakness, Mining Fatigue, Hunger, and their items drop when they die.

  • MOLOCH STIRS.
  • MOLOCH HAS RISEN.

The Blood Priest

Seller of everything an abduction needs

Found
Watching from the realm; turns his head to follow anyone who comes near
Trades
The Hood for 6 gold, the Cultist's Cudgel for 10, the Cultist's Shackles for 16, and Beef Tartare for 2
Secret stock
Festering Flesh, then the Heart of Darkness for the World Egg

A robed figure in black with burning red eyes, pictured holding out the Heart of Darkness. He sells everything you need to take someone: a sack to go over their head, a cudgel to daze them from behind, and shackles to close round their wrists. Buy everything he has and he shows you more. First comes Festering Flesh, which only the inhuman can keep down. Last of all comes the Heart of Darkness, and he'll only take the World Egg for it.

Wilder Blood Priests also walk the realm, taller than a man and harder to kill. They're evokers under the robes.

  • <Blood Priest> Pull it tight. Their breathing sounds better muffled.
  • <Blood Priest> From behind. Always from behind. Let them wonder who it was.
  • <Blood Priest> Beef. Yes. Let's call it beef.
  • <Blood Priest> No more Heaven for you. Don't worry. The view from down here is warmer.

The Friendly Stranger

A lovely bloke. Nothing to worry about. Hide your valuables.

Found
Moloch's realm, usually just behind you
Goes by
Friendly Stranger. Nobody calls him anything else. Bastard Thief
Stats
24 health. Walks very fast, for no particular reason
Drops
Nothing of yours, surely. Your whole inventory, and the Thief's Key

Just a friendly man in black who'd like to know the time. He walks right up to you, all smiles, and asks ever so politely. Checking your pockets afterwards would be rude.

If your things go missing after a chat with him, that's a coincidence. If you happen to kill him anyway, you might find them on him, along with an old brass key that opens iron doors and trapdoors without redstone. It snaps after a few uses. He must have found it somewhere.

He gets a bit touchy with people who have nothing on them, so it's best to carry something nice for him to... look at.

  • <Friendly Stranger> Excuse me mate, have you got the time?
  • <Friendly Stranger> Cheers, you're a star.
  • <Friendly Stranger> Thanks, I'll sell this lot down the market.
  • <Bastard Thief> Wasted my time, you skint muppet.
  • Bastard Thief robbed you! Kill it to get your things back.

Under a blood moon

The Overworld

Most nights are ordinary nights. Some aren't.

The Blood Moon

The night the animals turn

When
Some nights; the moon is held at midnight for as long as it lasts
Rules
Nobody can sleep through it

Under a blood moon even the livestock hunt you: cows, pigs, sheep, chickens, goats, rabbits and horses. The monsters come out armed and armoured, in random pieces of leather, chainmail, copper, gold and iron, and many carry spears.

Witches ride phantoms across the sky. Like every other monster they only appear in the dark, so a lit base keeps them away.

How it works

Kidnapping

On BaffoonMC you can capture another player, drag them away in chains, and even offer them to Moloch. Here's how it works, step by step, and every way it can end.

  1. Get the tools

    The Blood Priest in Moloch’s realm sells everything you need for gold. None of it can be crafted.

  2. Wear them down

    3 hearts or less

    You can only shackle a player who is badly hurt. Fight them first.

    3 hearts5 hearts if dazed

  3. Daze them from behind

    Hit a weakened player in the back with the Cudgel and they’re dazed for 3 seconds: slow, weak and dizzy. A dazed player can be shackled at up to 5 hearts.

    From behind3 seconds

  4. Shackle them

    Right-click them with the Shackles. They’re chained to you and can only wander 4 blocks before they’re dragged along. You walk a little slower.

    Lasts 3 minutesNo /home or /spawn

  5. Hood them

    Use the Hood on your captive. They see nothing, their name disappears, and nobody can tell who you’ve got. Hooded captives find it harder to struggle free.

    BlindNameless1.5× harder to escape

  6. Carry them

    Sneak and right-click your captive to throw them over your shoulder. Handy for stairs, boats and quick getaways.

    1.25× harder to escape

How it ends

Every capture ends one of these ways. The Shackles lose a use each time.

  1. Struggle free

    Sneak 30 times · 4 a second at most

    The captive taps sneak to struggle. After the first 25 seconds, every press fills the meter; stop and it drains. Fill it and the chain snaps.

  2. Rescued

    3 ♥

    Anyone who hurts the captor for 3 hearts breaks the chain. Friends can save you.

  3. Time runs out

    3:00

    After 3 minutes the chain gives way on its own. The captor has to keep the Shackles in their inventory the whole time.

  4. Sacrificed

    Drag a hooded captive into the fire pit at the top of Moloch’s pyramid. If nobody stops you in 10 seconds, Moloch takes them: they die and come back cursed, Moloch is fed, and you’re rewarded.

Fair play

  • No captures within 48 blocks of spawn.
  • After being freed you can’t be captured again for 3 minutes.
  • Logging out while captured kills you where you stand.
  • New players (under 5 hours played) can’t be sacrificed.
  • One sacrifice per captor per day, and the same player can’t be sacrificed again for 48 hours.

What you can become

Players

Not every being on BaffoonMC was made by the server. Some are what players become, and one is what they grow.

The Inhuman

Anyone who ate the Heart of Darkness

Becoming one
Eat the Heart of Darkness
Cure
The Angel Engine, which only the Peacekeeper sells
Tells
Bruised purple hearts on a black bar, and a sickly green hunger bar

Monsters leave the inhuman alone unless struck. They carry three extra hearts, and in Moloch's realm they have Fire Resistance and Speed. Raw meat feeds them, and rotten flesh, spider eyes and poisonous potatoes no longer make them sick. Every other food leaves them hungrier.

The living hate them. Livestock, wolves and cats attack. Iron golems hunt them. Villagers run unless the inhuman hides their face under a Hood, and then they charge more. Only zombie villagers trade freely. The inhuman can't sleep, the sun burns a bare head, and Heaven will never let them in again.

Pictured wearing the Black Filament, a parasite that latches onto the chest. It keeps its host alive with Regeneration, eats everything they eat, and won't come off until it's starved out.

  • <Blood Priest> He won't let you back into His house after this. Good. It's cold up there.

The Graced

Anyone who ate the Angel Engine

Becoming one
Eat the Angel Engine, the Heart of Darkness mended in gold. Only the Peacekeeper in Heaven sells it, for the World Egg
Losing it
Eat the Heart of Darkness and the light goes out
If you're inhuman
The Angel Engine cures you instead: you become human again, not Graced

The Graced hit the undead harder, a fifth more with every blow. Heaven’s Archangels leave them be, though God’s own host still fights them while He does. When they fall to three hearts or less, a Second Wind of Regeneration lifts them, once a minute. In Heaven they carry three extra hearts.

Grace and darkness can’t share a body. Choose one.

  • <Server> You are Graced. The dead fear your hand, Heaven’s Archangels know you, and when you fall, the light lifts you.

The Homunculus

A little wide-eyed thing, grown in a flask

Making one
Craft a Dragon Egg (the World Egg), a Tumour, a Tear of God and an Ember of Moloch. See the recipe
How many
One per player
Feeding
Tumours and eggs. Left unfed for a few days it grows slow; leave it longer and it rots away to a tumour

Use the flask on the ground and it climbs out. It never attacks anyone. Monsters and golems leave it alone, the sun doesn't burn it and water doesn't drown it. It makes its own small noises, and now and then it says what it's thinking in a little bubble over its head.

Right-click it for its menu: dress it, name it, feed it, put it back in its flask, and give it orders. Follow me, Wait here, Farm here (it harvests and replants ripe crops in your claim and puts the harvest in the nearest chest) or Guard here (it squeals when anyone else comes near and tells you who). Its nine pockets work whatever it's doing.

Inside its owner's claim nothing can hurt it. Outside, it can be killed, and it drops whatever it was carrying. Moloch would very much like to eat one. Those who let him are never quite the same again.

  • <Homunculus> I was nothing in a jar. Now I'm here. Thank you for that.
  • <Homunculus> Is the sun a big egg? When will it hatch?
  • <Homunculus> I'm right behind you! I'm always right behind you!
  • <Homunculus> When I grow up, I want to be a cow.
Pictures are rough poses built from each being's real skin or texture in the server pack. The Zephyrs and the Inhuman are drawn from their descriptions, and the Blood Moon is a scene rather than one creature.
